data.text: Interaction and perceptual designs are both important for usability in an XR system. These designs aim to create an illusion of reality to enhance presence, which is a sense of reality as if the user is in the real world. Creating this illusion is crucial for VR, while it is less significant but not totally insignificant for AR or MR.
points: Interaction and perceptual designs are both important for usability in an XR system.
XR systems create an illusion of reality to enhance presence.
Creating an illusion of reality is more crucial for VR than for AR or MR.

data.text: VR systems aim to fool a user's perception to create immersion, but human bodies and sensory organs are designed for the real world. VR generally provides sensory signals inconsistent with real-life experiences, which may lead to adaptation or cybersickness. Understanding human perception is necessary to design better systems or resolve flaws.
points: VR systems aim to fool a user's perception to create immersion.
Human bodies and sensory organs are designed for the real world, not virtual systems.
VR generally provides sensory signals inconsistent with real-life experiences.
Inconsistent stimulation may lead to adaptation or cybersickness.
Understanding human perception is necessary to design better systems or resolve flaws.

data.text: Perceptual psychology is the science of how the brain converts sensory stimulation into perceived phenomena. This knowledge is even more important for XR systems because they aim to extend the user's idea of reality. It provides guidelines for building better hardware and understanding user experiences by requiring knowledge of human physiology and how XR systems interfere with perceptual processes.
points: Perceptual psychology is the science of how the brain converts sensory stimulation into perceived phenomena.
This knowledge is even more important for XR systems because they aim to extend the user's idea of reality.
It provides guidelines for building better hardware and understanding the effects of an XR system on the user.
It requires knowledge of human physiology, experimental psychology theories, and how XR systems interfere with perceptual processes.

data.text: A sensor can refer to a device that converts energy into electrical signals or a human organ that converts a stimulus into neural impulses. Human senses are classified into six categories—vision, auditory, touch, balance, taste, and smell—based on their stimuli, receptors, and organs. Notably, balance is a sense that lacks a specific sense organ, unlike the other five senses.
points: Sensors can be devices that convert energy into electrical signals or human organs that convert stimuli into neural impulses.
The six human senses are vision, auditory, touch, balance, taste, and smell, each classified by their stimuli, receptors, and organs.
Balance is unique among the six senses because it does not have a specific sense organ.

data.text: Sensory system selectivity allows receptors to target particular stimuli and activate only when specific types arrive. While eyes use photoreceptors for visible light, mechanoreceptors sense motion, vibration, and gravitational force for hearing, touch, and balance. Additionally, touch includes thermoreceptors for temperature, balance identifies head orientation, and chemoreceptors detect chemical composition for taste and smell.
points: Sensory system selectivity means receptors target particular stimuli and activate only when those specific types arrive.
Eyes use photoreceptors to target visible light.
Mechanoreceptors sense motion, vibration, or gravitational force for hearing, touch, and balance.
Touch also involves thermoreceptors for temperature, and the balance sense identifies head orientation.
Chemoreceptors provide signals based on chemical composition for taste and smell.

data.text: Understanding human factors in XR systems requires knowledge of perceptual psychology, which includes the physiology of the senses. Humans have six senses: vision, auditory, balance, taste, smell, and touch. Sensory organs act as the hardware of sensing, using receptors like photoreceptors, chemoreceptors, and mechanoreceptors to receive stimuli.
points: Understanding human factors in XR systems requires knowledge of perceptual psychology.
The physiology of the senses is a part of perceptual psychology.
The six senses are vision, auditory, balance, taste, smell, and touch.
Sensory organs are the sensing hardware of the human body, using receptors like photoreceptors, chemoreceptors, and mechanoreceptors to receive stimuli.
